title: 山坡羊·潼关怀古
titlePy: Shān Pō Yáng · Tóngguān Huái Gǔ
titleEn: Thinking of the Past at Tongguan Pass (to the tune “Sheep on the Hillside”)
author: 张养浩
intro: Standing at a famous mountain pass, an old official looks toward the ruins of ancient capitals and reaches a blunt conclusion: when a dynasty rises, the people suffer; when it falls, the people suffer.
analysis: 这首小令是张养浩去关中救灾的路上，经过潼关时写的。开头三句写潼关的形势：群山像从四面聚拢过来，黄河的波涛像在发怒，潼关外有黄河、内有华山，地势非常险要。“聚”“怒”两个字把山和水写活了，好像有感情一样，这叫“拟人”。接着诗人望向西边的古都长安，心里起伏不平。秦朝、汉朝曾经在这里建起无数宫殿，如今全都变成了泥土。最后两句是全曲的中心，也是最有名的话：“兴，百姓苦；亡，百姓苦。”一个朝代兴起时，要大修宫殿、打仗，老百姓受苦；一个朝代灭亡时，战乱不断，老百姓还是受苦。不管谁当皇帝，吃苦的都是普通人。“怀古”就是借古代的事来表达对现实的看法。这六个字说出了很多人想说却没说出来的道理，所以流传了七百年。
analysisEn: Zhang Yanghao wrote this song on his way to bring famine relief to the Guanzhong region, when he passed through Tongguan, a strategic pass between the Yellow River and Mount Hua. The opening paints the place: the peaks crowd in as if gathering together, the waves of the Yellow River seem furious, and the road to the pass runs between river and mountains. The verbs “gather” and “rage” give the landscape feelings of its own — a device called nǐrén (personification). Then the poet looks west toward Chang’an, the old capital, and his mind is uneasy. The Qin and Han dynasties built countless palaces there, and now every one has turned to dust. The last two lines are the heart of the song and among the most quoted in Chinese: “Rise — the people suffer; fall — the people suffer.” When a dynasty rises, it builds palaces and fights wars on the people’s backs; when it falls, war and chaos crush them again. Whoever rules, ordinary people pay. This is what huáigǔ (“thinking of the past”) poems do: they look at history to say something about the present. Six plain characters put into words what many felt, and they have been repeated for seven hundred years.
background: Zhang Yanghao (1270–1329) was a Yuan official known for his honesty who retired early. In 1329, at nearly sixty, he accepted a post to fight a severe drought and famine in Shaanxi, and wrote this on the way; he died of exhaustion a few months later.
pronunciation: “望西都”的“都”读 dū（都城），“都做了土”的“都”读 dōu（全）。“经行处”的“行”读 xíng。“宫阙”的“阙”读 què。“踌躇”读 chóu chú。“兴，百姓苦”的“兴”读 xīng（兴盛），不读 xìng。
version: 采用统编语文教材九年级下册文本，全曲九句，此处完整收录。“山坡羊”是曲牌，“潼关怀古”是题目，“中吕”是宫调。张养浩同曲牌另有多首怀古之作。

lines.lit: Peaks and ridges as if gathering,
lines.en: The peaks crowd in from every side,

lines.py: shān hé biǎo lǐ tóng guān lù
lines.lit: mountains and river outside and inside — the road to Tongguan.
lines.en: river without, mountains within — this is the road through Tongguan.

lines.py: wàng xī dū, yì chóu chú
lines.lit: Gazing at the western capital, my mind hesitates.
lines.en: I look toward the old western capital, and my heart is troubled.

lines.py: shāng xīn qín hàn jīng xíng chù
lines.lit: Heartbroken at where Qin and Han once passed,
lines.en: It hurts to see where the Qin and Han once marched:

lines.py: gōng què wàn jiān dōu zuò le tǔ
lines.lit: palaces of ten thousand rooms have all turned to earth.
lines.en: ten thousand palace halls, every one turned to dust.

lines.py: xīng, bǎi xìng kǔ, wáng, bǎi xìng kǔ
lines.lit: Rising — the common people suffer; falling — the common people suffer.
lines.en: When an empire rises, the people suffer; when it falls, the people suffer.

words.note: 峦：连绵的山。今天书面语仍说“峰峦起伏”。
本义是生气，这里形容波涛汹涌，今天也说“怒放”“怒吼”。
这里指潼关外有黄河、内有华山。今天还说“表里如一”。
古代军事要地，在黄河拐弯处。
今天多指犹豫不决，如“踌躇不前”；也说“踌躇满志”（得意）。
指秦汉两朝在这里建都、活动过的地方。
阙：宫门前的高台，代指宫殿。
现代汉语说“兴盛”“兴旺”。读 xìng 时是“高兴”的“兴”。

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 群山好像从四面聚拢，写出潼关地势的险要和雄伟。
imagery.en: Mountains crowding in from all sides show how steep and commanding the pass is.

imagery.name: 黄河
imagery.zh: 波涛“如怒”，黄河好像带着怒气，也暗暗呼应诗人心中的不平。
imagery.en: The “raging” Yellow River seems angry — echoing the poet’s own indignation.

imagery.name: 关
imagery.zh: 潼关是历代兵家必争之地，见证了无数朝代的兴亡。
imagery.en: Tongguan, fought over by army after army, has witnessed the rise and fall of dynasty after dynasty.

imagery.name: 宫阙
imagery.zh: 秦汉万间宫殿都变成了土，说明再强大的王朝也会消失，而百姓的苦却没变。
imagery.en: Ten thousand Qin and Han palaces gone to dust: empires vanish, but the people’s suffering stays.
